en: As long as within the heart, inside,
and toward the edges of the east, forward,
an eye looks out to Zion,
our hope is not yet lost,
the hope two thousand years old,
to be a free people in our land,
the land of Zion and Jerusalem.
notes: This is the anthem's text (two stanzas), not Imber's 1878 poem 'Tikvatenu', whose first stanza and refrain differ (from memory, to be checked against the 1886 printing: the refrain spoke of returning to the land of our fathers, the city where David encamped). The credit line should say so.
line 1.2: 'homiyyah' is literally 'murmurs, stirs, moans'; rendered 'yearns'.
line 1.3: 'pa'atei mizrach' is literally 'the corners/edges of the east'; 'kadimah' is both 'eastward' and 'forward'.
Zion and Jerusalem stay as names in en; romanized as tsiyyon, yerushalayim (here with the prefix: virushalayim).
